extracted.intended_audience: government officials (Secretaries of State/War), diplomats, military commanders, historians
extracted.subtask_description: Presidential instructions and policy statements (diplomatic, military, and administrative) issued during the early Civil War period covering blockade policy, recognition, treatment of privateers, acceptance of volunteer regiments, suspension of habeas corpus, and related confidential dispatch handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: No intercourse with insurgent commissioners (official or unofficial)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will in any event desist from all intercourse whatever, unofficial as well as official, with the British Government, so long as it shall continue intercourse of either kind with the domestic enemies of this country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unofficial intercourse is liable to be construed as recognition and may be more injurious because it could resolve points without US knowledge; desist from any intercourse while the British government communicates with Confederate agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base proceedings on parliamentary debates beyond seeking explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: You will base no proceedings on parliamentary debates further than to seek explanations when necessary and communicate them to this department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely only on necessary explanations from debates; avoid acting on newspaper reports or parliamentary debate summaries except to request clarification and inform the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignore reported Anglo‑French 'understanding' until direct communication
rubrics_metrics.description: It is left doubtful here whether the proposed unofficial intercourse has yet actually begun... Lord John Russell has informed us of an understanding between the British and French governments that they will act together in regard to our affairs. You will take no notice of that or any other alliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not proactively base policy or protests on reported alliances; respond when European governments communicate directly with the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blockade as legal means to suppress insurrection (must be maintained to be respected)
rubrics_metrics.description: By our own laws and the laws of nations, this Government has a clear right to suppress insurrection. An exclusion of commerce from national ports which have been seized by the insurgents, in the equitable form of blockade, is the proper means to that end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insist blockade is to be respected if not maintained by competent force, but assert that the blockade is now and will continue to be so maintained and thus expected to be respected by foreign powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revoke exequatur / dismiss foreign agents who join insurgents
rubrics_metrics.description: We have already revoked the exequatur of a Russian consul who had enlisted in the military service of the insurgents, and we shall dismiss or demand the recall of every foreign agent, consular or diplomatic, who shall either disobey the Federal laws or disown the Federal authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce diplomatic consequences (revocation, dismissal, demand for recall) against foreign representatives who actively support the insurgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and belligerent rights criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: It is direct recognition to publish an acknowledgment of the sovereignty and independence of a new power. It is direct recognition to receive its ambassadors, ministers, agents, or commissioners officially. A concession of belligerent rights is liable to be construed as a recognition of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid acts (official reception, published acknowledgment, concessions) that could be construed as recognition; treat any concession of belligerent rights as potentially tantamount to recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of privateers / enemy citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: As to the treatment of privateers in the insurgent service, you will say that this is a question exclusively our own. We treat them as pirates. They are our own citizens, or persons employed by our citizens, preying on the commerce of our country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assert domestic jurisdiction over privateers; note that if foreign powers recognize them as lawful belligerents, international remedies exist. Propose accession to the Paris Declaration abolishing privateering to avoid these difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark certain dispatches confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper is for your own guidance only, and not to be read or shown to any one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where indicated, keep dispatches strictly confidential and do not circulate beyond the intended recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorize suspension of the writ of habeas corpus where necessary for public safety
rubrics_metrics.description: If at any point on or in the vicinity of any military line which is now or which shall be used between the city of New York and the city of Washington you find resistance which renders it necessary to suspend the writ of habeas corpus for the public safety, you personally, or through the officer in command at the point where resistance occurs, are authorized to suspend that writ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empower commanders to suspend habeas corpus locally where resistance threatens public safety; exercise sparingly and only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for accepting volunteer regiments into Federal service
rubrics_metrics.description: The government has already accepted ten regiments from the State of Indiana. ... to be received into the volunteer service of the United States according to the 'Plan of Organization' in the General Orders of the War Department, No.15. When they report to Major‑General McClellan in condition to pass muster according to that order, and with the approval of the Secretary of War to be indorsed hereon, and left in his department, I direct that the whole six, or any smaller number of such regiments, be received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regiments must conform to the Plan of Organization (Gen. Orders No. 15), pass muster before the designated commander, and have Secretary of War approval; acceptance often requires concurrence of the state governor and may be limited by specified quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and conditions for state‑presented regiments
rubrics_metrics.description: If it can be received with the approval of your department and the consent of the Governor of Massachusetts I shall indeed be much gratified. ... I think it entirely safe to accept a fifth regiment from Michigan, and with your approbation I should say a regiment presented by Col. T. B. W. Stockton... will be received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptances of additional regiments depend on departmental approval, governor consent, testimonial checks, and assessments of readiness; the President recommends consultation with relevant officials before receiving units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of war powers and emergency measures to preserve the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: So viewing the issue, no choice was left but to call out the war power of the government, and so to resist force employed for its destruction by force for its preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When insurrection threatens the existence of the Union, invoke war powers (militia calls, blockades, enlarging forces) as necessary; recognize that some measures may be subject to later congressional ratification but are justified by public necessity.
